† * 341. SHRI  ANANTRAY DEVSHANKER DAVE:  Will  the Minister of 
RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:

Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh and what arc the targets fixed under the scheme; and 
(c) what is the State-wise number of persons including those States targeted to 
be provided with jobs by the end of year 2000? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) to (c) The Stat ement showing State-wise  allocation of funds 
under the Employment Assurance Scheme during the years 1997-98, 1998-99, 
1999-2000 and 2000-2001 is enclosed as Statement-I. (See below) The Scheme

universalised in 1997-98 to cover all the rural Panchayat samitis of the country.

released on receipt of proposals from the Districts after utilisation of 50% of the 
total available funds. As such, allocation of

Status of Tehri Hydro Power Project 
342. SHRI MANOHAR KANT DHYANI: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred Question 1974 given in the Rajya Sabha 
on 9th August, 2000 and state: 
(a) as to which State will be the 'Home State' in the case of Tehri 
Hydro Power Project after the newly created State of Uttaranchal; 
and 
(b) which State will have the right to receive electricity at the rate 
of 12 percent of royalty or 20 percent of the production cost? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SURESH PRABHU): (a) and (b) Tehri 
Hydro-electric Project Stage-I (1000 MW) is a multipurpose project. The entire 
irrigation component of the project is being funded by the Government of Uttar 
Pradesh. Government of U.P. is also contributing 25% of the equity towards 
the power component of the project, in lieu of which they will receive 25% of 
the power generated from the project (after taking into account 12% 
†Original notice of the Question was received in Hindi. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA       [13 December, 2000] 
free power). The sharing benefits accruing from the Tehri Project as 
prescribed in the Article of Association of THDC is given below: 
(i) The entire irrigation benefits shall be available to Govt, of Uttar 
Pradesh in lieu of 100% cost bcarancc of "Irrigation 
Sector". 
(ii) 12% of generated power at bus bar shall be available to Govt, of Uttar 
Pradesh free of cost as royalty in lieu of use of natural resources of 
home state. 
(iii) 25% of the remaining 88% of generated power at bus bar shall be 
allocated to Govt, of Uttar Pradesh in lieu of 25% contribution of 
"Power Sector" by Govt, of Uttar Pradesh. 
(iv) The remaining 66% of generated power at bus bar shall be in the 
central pool in lieu of 75% of cost sharing of power sector by Govt, 
of India and shall be shared between Govt, of India and Govt, of 
Uttar Pradesh in accordance with the standard formula evolved by the 
Govt, of India. 
Further, the guidelines for allocation of power from the Central Sector 
hydel projects envisages supply of 12% power free of cost to the States of the 
region (including the State where the pr oject is located) where distress like 
submergence and dislocation of population, is caused. The allocation of 
balance power, according to these guidelines, is to be distributed amongst the 
States/UTs of the Region, based on consumption of energy and availing of 
Central Plan assistance during the last five years; both factors being give equal 
weightage. 
The allocation of power to Uttaranchal and Uttar Pradesh would need to be 
decided keeping in view the guidelines referred to above and apportionment 
of rights and liabilities between these States in accordance with the provisions 
of Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.

Funds to private sector companies for rural development 
343. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any scheme to allow private sector companies to receive 
funds for rural development; 
(b) if so, the amount received for rural development during the last two 
years; and 
(c) the number of schemes approved under this policy? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) to (c) Under the Scheme of National Fund for Rural 
Development, which was set up in February, 1984, funds are received for rural 
development from individual, corporate and non-corporate bodies. Projects 
under the Scheme may be executed through an Implementing Agency 
recommended by the donor. The Agency so recommended to receive such funds 
for implementing the Project should have legal status of (a) a Company 
incorporated under section 25 of the Companies* Act. 1956; or (b) a Corporation 
established by or under a Central/State Act concerned with the development of 
rural areas; or (c) a Society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 
or under any law corresponding to that Act in force in any part of India; or (d) an 
irrevocable public charitable trust within the meaning of, and duly constituted 
and registered under the Income-tax Act, 1961. 
The funds received during 1998-99 and 1999-2000 under the Scheme 
amounted to Rs. 75.15 lakhs and Rs. 66.10 lakhs, respectively. So far, 58 
proposals have been approved under this Scheme.

Law to detect Foreign Nationals in Voters List 
* 345. DR.  (SMT.) JOYASREE GOSWAMI MAHANTA: Will the 
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any law regarding detection of names of foreign 
nationals in voters list and their deportation from the country which is applicable 
only in Assam as against a totally different law known as Foreigners Act, which 
is applicable in the rest of the country; 
(b) if so, the reasons for this discrimination in regard to Assam; 
(c) whether Government have any proposal to make IMDT Act applicable 
throughout the country; and 
(d) whether Government have taken any steps to repeal IMDT Act from 
Assam and if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): (a) to (d) The Illegal 
Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, P983 was enacted in 1 983 for 
detection and deportation of illegal migrants who had entered into India on or after 
25.3.71. The Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983 is 
applicable to the entire country although it has been notified as of now for the 
State of Assam only. The Act was enacted in the background of the Assam 
agitation for detection and deportation of illegal migrants. 
The Government has no proposal to extend the Illegal Migrants 
(Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983 to the rest of the country. A 
9

under consideration of the Government.

* 346. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to refer to answer to Starred Question 71, given in 
the Rajya Sabha on 23rd November, 2000 and state: 
(a) whether funds of Rs. 38.90 crores  under Accelerated Rural Water 
Supply Programme (ARWSP) and Rs. 20 crores under Sub-Mission projects 
released by Government to West Bengal have anything to do with the recent 
floods; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) and (b) The funds released under ARWSP and for Sub-Mission 
projects are for providing safe drinking water supply facilities to rural habitations. 
Even though the release of Rs. 38.90 crore under the ARWSP and Rs. 20.00 crore 
for the Sub-Mission projects are not speci fically meant for flood relief, the 
activities taken up with these funds in flood affected areas would certainly 
benefit the affected rural population.

Security environment around India 
348. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the security environment in India's immediate and extended 
neighbourhood is continuing to deteriorate; 
(b) if sot whether any efforts have been made to monitor and analyse the 
development in the region; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): (a) 
to (c) As a consequence of the inter-play of a host of factors including fast 
technological developments culminating in the Revolution in Military Affairs 
(RMA) and other factors such as international and cross-border terrorism aided and 
abetted both by the State and non-State actors, religious fanaticism, proliferation of 
weapons of mass destruction etc. the security environment in India's immediate 
and extended neighbourhood remains complex. Government monitors and 
analyses all such developments on a continuous basis and take appropriate 
measures to ensure the security and uphold the territorial integrity of the nation. It 
would,'however not be in the national interest to divulge further details in this 
regard.

Priority to rural development and rural poor 
*349. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH: W ill the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to give priority to 
rural development and emphasis on rural poor especially on rural connectivity, 
water supply and their housing from the current financial year; 
(b) if so, the amount sanctioned under the Central Schemes during the 
current financial year, State-wise and item-wise; and 
(c) what is the actual disbursement against each item till date? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) In order to impart greater momentum to the provision of basic 
services in the rural areas, the Government, have, in the current year, launched 
a new Scheme, the Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY), to undertake 
time-bound programmes to fulfil the critical needs of these areas. 
An allocation of Rs. 5000 crore has been separately earmarked for the 
purpose in the Union Budget, 2000-2001, out of which Rs. 2500 crore has 
been earmarked to commence a nation-wide programme of constructing rural 
roads and improving rural connectivity. The remaining amount has been 
earmarked for the other five components viz. Primary Health, Primary 
Education, shelter, Drinking Water and Nutrition, of the PMGY. Under the 
Scheme, Central Assistance is to be provided to the States/Union Territories for 
implementing specific projects in these sectors. 
(b) and (c) Details are given in the Statement.

MISS MABEL REBELLO:

(a) whether Government's announcement to issue National Identity Card to all

2609. SHRI R.K. ANAND: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the  number of States  which  have  unbundled  their State 
Electricity Board; 
(b) the reasons for not implementing power reforms in many States: 
107 

RAJYA SABHA       [13 December, 2000] 
(c) whether Government have set up any contingency plan to tackle the 
situation arising because of unbundling of SEBs; and 
(d) whether the unbundling of SEBs would not increase the cost of 
generation and distribution of power and hence putting more burden in 
consumers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) to (d) The States of Orissa, 
Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka, and Rajasthan have 
unbundled their State Electricity Boards. Several States have taken a decision 
to undertake power sector reforms. 14 States (Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar 
Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Gujarat, 
Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Delhi and Punjab) have 
since notified/ constituted SERCs, with a view to undertake rationalisation of 
electricity tariff and to bring about transparency in relation to tarrif and 
subsidies. 
As a part of the strategy to give impetus to reforms and restructuring in 
the power sector, the Central Government has entered into Memorandum of 
Agreement (MoA) with the States of Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Madhya 
Pradesh, to support their reform efforts. 
Unbundling of SEBs into separate entities for generation, transmission 
and distribution aims at bringing in greater accountability and improved 
performance in terms of efficiency a nd competition and in turn to ensure 
reliable power supply to all consumers at reasonable prices.

Seismological Study of Then Dam 
2613. DR. KARAN SINGH: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether a sesimological study has been conducted to determine the 
safe height of Tehri Dam. if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether seismologists and geologists often express concern about 
the seismic danger presented by Tehri Dam; if so, what steps have been 
taken by Government to reassure about the seismic safety of the dam; and 
(c) the expenditure so far incurred on the dam and the progress so far 
made in construction thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) and (b) The Government had 
considered indepth the seismic safety of the Tehri Dam and the detailed 
seismology studies carried out by the Geological Survey of India. 
Department of Earthquake Engineering of the Roorkec University and the 
Russian experts assisted by the Natio nal Geophysical Research Institute, 
Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology for determining the safe height of 
Tehri Dam, before according approval to the implementation of the Tehri 
Dam and Hydro-electric Power Project (1000 MW) in March, 1994. 
In view of the continuing concern relating to seismic safety of the Tehri 
Dam, a Group of Experts was constituted in June, 1996 to further examine 
the issue of seismic safety of Tehri Dam. This Group in its report concluded 
that the design of the dam was safe  to withstand the Maximum Credible 
Earthquake.

Statement 
The Mumbai Declaration 
I 
—  It is generally well recognized th at humanity faces two major crises 
of worsening energy situation and increasing degradation of 
environment. 
—  It is clear that a great deal of destruction of the environment is 
directly related to the production, transportation and consumption of 
finite non-renewable resources like fossil fuel.

Of the 6.1 billion people, 4.9 billion people living in the development 
world face unprecedented problems of declining energy resources. 
At least 2 billion people in the south arc energy refugees surviving on 
firewood, which consumes large amounts of the lifetime of women in 
countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America. 
At the same time, the forest and tree covers in these parts of the 
world are depicting very fast driving these people to the edge of the 
precipice. 
II 
Recognizing that the global situ ation concerning fossil fuel are 
shrinking and that nuclear power is being denounced by a majority of 
nations and people. 
Knowing that the present devastation of the global and local 
environments is already making the lives of millions of people 
intolerable. 
Believing that the present situation cannot continue for a long period 
of lime. 
We have prepared this Mumbai Declaration at the end of the 
international conference on Sustainable Energy & Environment. 
The Declaration, at the outset, em phasizes that the path for humanity 
in the 21st century for sustainable development is to tap the 
renewable resources first in the developing countries and in time the 
world over. 
Already, many countries and organizations have undertaken the task 
of developing biogas plants, solar energy systems-photovoltaic and 
other simple solar systems such as solar cookers, dryers, etc. 
There arc innumerable other energy resources being developed 
worldwide such as biogas plants and wind farms, etc.

—  There is a great deal of research  and development necessary for the 
area of solar power satellite and lunar power satellites. 
—  The other renewable resources of energy include gethermal, tidal, etc. 
III 
—  Therefore, wc recommend global and national policies concerning 
renewable energy developments while at the same time ensure the 
environ menial protection. 
—  For this purpose, vast investments in all these related areas should be 
necessary in the United Nations, other international agencies. 
Government, business and industries. 
—  There should be a people's movement for the development of small 
and sustainable energy development projects. 
—  The most important item related to renewable energy is to mobilize 
the people of the world for energy conservation, energy efficiency 
and utilisation of all energy forms by setting up priorities. 
Ultimately, it is the last 30% of the people of the planet who should be 
protected from the energy deprivation. 
CONCLUSION 
For several centuries now, the number of people living as energy refugees 
has been escalating geometrically. Recognizing that energy is the key to 
survival, development and progress, it is the fundamental responsibility of 
humanity to move towards large scale development of renewable energy 
resources all over the planet in every country. The situation is grim and 
pathetic and if the trends continue at the present rate of decline, wc shall face 
a disaster of ah unprecedented order. Therefore, wc owe a responsibility not 
only to present generation but for many generations to come. Let the dreams 
of our children be realized by comm itting ourselves to the cause of the 
development of sustainable energy so that long after wc are gone, we leave 
behind a good life for all those who will traverse this beautiful earth.

employees/officers? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) No, Sir. The 'Annapuma' Scheme has been launched w.e.f. 1st 
April, 2000 to provide 10 Kgs. of foodgrains free of cost to those aged people 
who though eligible for pensions under National Old Age Pension Scheme 
(NOAPS), are not getting the same for th e present. The allocation under this 
Scheme during the current year is Rs. 100 crores out of which Rs. 82.04 crores 
has already been released to 20 States/UTs. 
The States/UTs arc in the process of implementing the Scheme in their 
respective jurisdiction. Four States have since lifted the foodgrains from the FCI 
for distribution. However, a few States like Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and 
Haryana have expressed their inability to implement the Scheme due to non-
availability of prospective beneficiaries. These States have already covered the 
remaining eligible NO APS beneficiaries under their own State Schemes for 
old age pension. The remaining States/UTs are in the process of the required 
conditionalities to receive funds. 
(b) Docs not arise. 
(c) While the Union Ministry of Rural Development are responsible 
for the Scheme at the Central level, the State Food & Civil Supplies 
Department arc the Nodal Departments for implementing the same in the 
States. Funds under the Scheme are released by the Centre in one instalment to 
the State Nodal Departments who have then to tic up the release of foodgrains, 
district-wise, with the FCI. The District Collector is responsible for the 
collection of foodgrains from the nearest FCI godown for distribution to 
beneficiaries through Fair Price shops. 
203 

RAJYA SABHA        [13 December, 2000] 
While no report in regard to misuse of funds and the like have so far been 
received, in order to ensure that the bene fits reach the needy, the guidelines on 
the Programme arc explicit in respect of the role of the Gram Panchayats in 
providing wide publicity to the Scheme and disseminating information as to 
the procedure for securing benefits under the same. The Guidelines also provide 
that the selection of beneficiaries as well as the distribution of entitlement Cards 
take place in the Gram Sabha Meetings and that the lists of the beneficiaries, so 
selected, are displayed in the Gram Panchayats. A detailed accounting system 
has also been prescribed in the Guidelines. Funds arc to be released (by the 
Ministry of Rural Development) to th e State Governments subject to their 
furnishing necessary Utilisation Certificates for the preceding year, duly vetted by 
the Accountant General of the State concerned. The State Authorities arc to 
release monies to the FCI, based on re ports received from the FCI in regard 
to the position of lifting of foodgrains, duly verified with independent reports 
received from the Collector's Office. The State Governments arc required to report 
allocation and lifting, distri ct-wise, every Quarter, to  the Union Ministry of 
Rural Development.
